name: Proxmox_VE_Topology
description: Cluster, node and guest topology for Proxmox VE: cluster to node, node to guest.
technicalNotes:
Emits two kinds of edge. Cluster to node, type "Cluster". Node to guest, type "Compute", which is the edge that matters: it lets a node's alerts explain the alerts of the guests it hosts.

Guests are matched to their own LogicMonitor resources by MAC address, read from the guest config (net0 and friends). This works because LogicMonitor already keys a monitored Linux resource on its MAC addresses, so the two ERIs meet with no name matching -- a Proxmox guest called "KTV" whose resource is called "KTV - PiKaraoke" still connects. It is the same identity VMware_vSphere_VirtualMachine_Topology uses. A guest with no readable MAC falls back to a synthesised key, as the VMware module does.

A guest is drawn only if it matches a resource: the portal does not render a vertex that matches nothing (confirmed 2026-09-23 -- an unmonitored LXC guest's edge was emitted and never drawn). So a guest appears on the map only once it is monitored as its own resource AND that resource's predef.externalResourceID carries the guest's MAC, which LogicMonitor's own discovery supplies over SNMP. A guest that cannot answer SNMP, such as a Home Assistant OS appliance, has no MAC in its ERI and stays off the map even when monitored.

Nodes cannot be matched that way. Proxmox exposes no hardware UUID and no MAC for a node anywhere in its API, so the node key is synthesised from the cluster and node names, and the companion PropertySource addERI_Proxmox_VE stamps the identical key on each node's own resource. A node whose resource has not run that PropertySource matches nothing, so by the same rule it is not drawn, and its alerts cannot explain its guests'. On the one-resource-per-cluster layout that docs/INSTALL.md recommends, only the node carrying the token runs the PropertySource; setting the token on every node makes every node match, at the duplication cost INSTALL section 4.1 describes.

Cost: one /cluster/status, one /cluster/resources per type, and one config read per guest. That last is O(guests), which DESIGN section 2 rules out for a metric module -- but this runs hourly rather than every five minutes, and the MAC is available nowhere else, since /cluster/resources carries no network detail.

This is the only module in the suite that cannot be compiled or run outside a Collector. LogicMonitor's own topology scripts do all their work through com.logicmonitor.mod.Snippets -- eriPreProcessor for key normalisation, isMac for validation, generateTopology for the output format -- and reimplementing those would mean inventing a format LogicMonitor does not fully document. The build emits it to dist/scripts/collector-only/ for that reason.
